assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a new boson at ATLAS and CMS, with properties consistent with the Standard Model Higgs, is a clear, concrete discovery of nature and the experimental completion of the electroweak sector. The 2013 prize honoured the theory; the experimental discovery itself has not been recognised. It is the kind of clue from nature that matters most to me.
assessment.attribution: The decisive experimental leadership is the conception and construction of the two detectors and collaborations; Della Negra and Virdee (CMS) and Jenni (ATLAS) are the natural founding-spokesperson figures. Thousands contributed, so any three names are a compromise, and a fair configuration is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by two experiments and by a decade of coupling measurements at the LHC. Interpretation is stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit among thousands of collaborators and the choice of spokespersons versus other key figures is contentious.
Whether the committee wishes to honour a collaboration-scale discovery with individual names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced precision full-sky CMB maps that fixed the age, geometry and composition of the universe and cemented the Lambda-CDM model, including strong evidence for dark energy and dark matter budgets. This directly bears on what I find existentially compelling. It builds on the COBE prize (2006) but is a distinct, transformative step.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission as PI, Page was a core instrument builder and Spergel the leading analysis and cosmological-interpretation figure. Credit is reasonably clean, though the Planck team and others share the later precision story.
assessment.maturity: Results were confirmed and refined by Planck and ground-based experiments. Mature and stable; recognition is timely to late.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier COBE recognition and with Planck may make the committee view it as incremental.
Selection of three from a large WMAP team.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea and brought to extreme precision by Ye, reaches fractional uncertainty near 1e-18. It enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a likely redefinition of the second. It is a clear invention with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice clock; Jun Ye drove it to record accuracy and many-body-clock regimes. Two laureates is a clean configuration, although Hall and Hansch (comb) and Wineland (ion clocks) were already recognised.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs worldwide confirm performance and clock comparisons. Mature, with the redefinition of the second still pending, which makes it timely.
uncertainties: Other contributors to optical clock development (e.g. ion clock groups, strontium groups, Ye's JILA colleagues) may deserve credit.
Whether it is seen as too close to prior comb and ion-trap prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray (BeppoSAX), optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts resolved the decades-old puzzle of their distance, established their cosmological origin and opened the study of the most energetic explosions. It is a discovery driven directly by observation and changed astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX detections of the X-ray afterglow; Kulkarni's team secured the optical and radio redshift and counterpart work. Others (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Galama, Metzger) also contributed, so allocation is not entirely clean, but the proposed trio is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed, with Swift and Fermi building a vast body of results. Mature; the connection to gravitational-wave multi-messenger events adds weight.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Dutch, Italian and US groups, and the late Jan van Paradijs, is delicate.
The Nobel rules limit awards to the living, constraining otherwise valid candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators by Kane and Mele, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells by Molenkamp's group, opened a major field of topological matter with a prediction confirmed by experiment. It is the sort of theory validated by nature that I value.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele gave the decisive theoretical insight; Molenkamp led the first experimental realisation. Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (HgTe proposal) and 3D TI experimentalists such as Hasan are not in this list, so there is an unresolved credit question.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations (HgTe, Bi-based materials, ARPES) and extensive follow-up. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: The exclusion of the HgTe theory proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and 3D topological insulator experiments weakens a complete credit picture.
Overlap with the 2016 topological phase-transition prize may be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bistritzer and MacDonald's prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulation and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene by Jarillo-Herrero's group created the moire materials field. It is an unusually clean pairing of prediction and observation.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer-MacDonald supplied the theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group the decisive experiments. Others (Cao, Fatemi, Dean, Santos-Neto-Castro, Kim) share the story and the three-name configuration omits them.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many labs within a few years, though the nature of the superconductivity is still debated. Interpretation is not fully stable; timing is early-to-fair.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Credit for the first author Yuan Cao and for earlier twist work remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos by IceCube opened a new window onto the cosmos and identified the TXS 0506+056 blazar and Galactic plane as sources. Observation-driven and conceptually clear, with a real existential reach.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the principal conceiver and leader of IceCube, but the discovery is a very large-collaboration achievement and the list credits only one name, which makes a fair configuration doubtful.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple IceCube analyses and multi-messenger follow-up, but source identification is still developing. Reasonably timely, somewhat early for a complete picture.
uncertainties: Single credited name omits important figures in neutrino astronomy such as Learned, Markov or others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed ion-trap quantum gates and laid the foundations for quantum simulation with cold atoms, concepts now realised in major experiments. Lasting and original impact on quantum information and AMO physics.
assessment.attribution: The two are the clear theoretical originators of these proposals and a two-person configuration is clean. Experimental realisers (Wineland, Blatt, Bloch) are not on this entry.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed in many trapped-ion and atom platforms. Mature, but the field is still unfolding, and the 2022 and 2012 prizes already recognised neighbouring work.
uncertainties: Theory contribution recognised without the experimental teams that demonstrated it.
Possible overlap with other quantum computing entries on the list and with earlier prizes.
